blocks.md: **Four tools carry almost all of the matrix algebra in econometrics: the reversal rules for transposes and inverses, the conditions for an inverse to exist, the partitioned inverse, and the trace. With them you can read $\mathbf{b} = (\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{y}$, $\mathrm{Var}(\mathbf{b}) = \sigma^2(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X})^{-1}$ and $E[\mathbf{e}'\mathbf{e}] = (n-K)\sigma^2$ line by line.**

[Matrix Algebra Identities](note:matrix-algebra-identities): $(AB)' = B'A'$ and $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$. These are why $X'X$ is symmetric and why its inverse is too. Write dimensions under every term — it catches most mistakes.

[Invertibility and Determinants](note:invertibility-and-determinants): for a square matrix, a nonzero determinant, full rank, independent columns and no zero eigenvalue are all the same condition. In regression the square matrix is $\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}$, invertible exactly when the regressors are not linearly dependent — the identification condition in [Econ 430 L1 Simple Linear Regression](note:econ-430-l1-simple-linear-regression).

[Partitioned Matrices](note:partitioned-matrices): split $\mathbf{X} = [\mathbf{X}_1\ \mathbf{X}_2]$ and the partitioned inverse hands you $(\mathbf{X}_2'\mathbf{M}_1\mathbf{X}_2)^{-1}$ — the algebra of the [Frisch-Waugh-Lovell Theorem](note:frisch-waugh-lovell-theorem), which is how [Econ 424 L2 Between-Group Inequality](note:econ-424-l2-between-group-inequality) justifies detrending.

[Trace of a Matrix](note:trace-of-a-matrix): the cyclic property turns a scalar quadratic form into a trace, so $E[\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}'\mathbf{M}\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}] = \sigma^2\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf{M})$. For an idempotent matrix trace equals rank, which is where $N - K$ in $\widehat{\sigma}^2$ comes from ([Sampling Distribution of OLS](note:sampling-distribution-of-ols)).

blocks.title: 2. Is $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\4&2\end{pmatrix}$ invertible?
blocks.md: No: the determinant is $4 - 4 = 0$; the second column is half the first. → [Invertibility and Determinants](note:invertibility-and-determinants)

blocks.title: 3. Simplify $\big((X'X)^{-1}X'\big)'$.
blocks.md: $X(X'X)^{-1}$, using $(AB)' = B'A'$ and the symmetry of $(X'X)^{-1}$. → [Matrix Algebra Identities](note:matrix-algebra-identities)

blocks.title: 4. $\mathbf{P}$ is a $5\times5$ projection onto a 2-dimensional subspace. What is $\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{P})$?
blocks.md: $5 - 2 = 3$: trace is linear, and for an idempotent matrix trace equals rank. → [Trace of a Matrix](note:trace-of-a-matrix)

blocks.title: 5. True or false: $\mathrm{tr}(ABC) = \mathrm{tr}(ACB)$.
blocks.md: False in general. The trace is cyclic, $\mathrm{tr}(ABC) = \mathrm{tr}(BCA) = \mathrm{tr}(CAB)$, but you cannot swap two factors. → [Trace of a Matrix](note:trace-of-a-matrix)

sections.heading: What to be able to do

blocks.md:
1. Transpose and invert products without reversing the order wrongly.
2. State the equivalent conditions for invertibility, and connect them to identification.
3. Use the partitioned inverse to get the block of $(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X})^{-1}$ for a subset of regressors.
4. Use the cyclic trace property to compute $E[\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}'\mathbf{M}\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}]$.
